chapter: Church, Bel Canto and the return to music
title: Bel Canto Foundation: helping musicians off heroin with prayers and music
summary: She helped addict musicians by keeping them with her and having them play drum parts she wrote.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: That was your life then? When did you start the Bel Canto Foundation?
I don't know what year it was but it was during that period while I was praying.

I decided that I wanted to help the few - well, after comparing rock I said the few - few musicians that were using dope, jazz musicians that were using dope. I decided I'd like to help them and so I went on out on my own with a method of my own. I had success with two.
Prayers and music, either give them Psalms to

read or write something. Like I had a drummer that was on it and his wife timed him. It took him 5 minutes to go home. He'd come here 8 o'clock in the morning and I'd just keep him in the house. See, a dope addict, anyone on heroin, they're like a baby. So I'd keep them with me all day. If I had to go, I'd say, "Come on, we'll go to the Five and Ten." One time I took him to the Five and Ten and I forgot to give him breakfast. I said, oh, I hope he doesn't steal anything while we're in here. Sure enough, he told me this two or three years later. He said, "Remember when you took me to the Five and Ten. I was so hungry I was getting ready to steal some candy. I looked on the floor and saw a quarter." He bought the candy. I said, "Man, I was praying for you that you didn't steal anything." ... This guy, it must have been in his mind or something because he was cured so very fast, but later on I had to take him to someone for injections and whatnot to counteract what he was doing. The first night I had him here in the house he began to want a fix and so I said, "I just wrote a drum part." I wrote and I wrote and I said, "Dig this." He said, "Yeah." I said, "Well, play it." He had a pad, and ... He played it and he forgot. Everytime that happened I said, "Hey," and I'd write something else. That worked on him I noticed that night because it took his mind off completely... or else the staff. They gave him was so weak.

night he didn't have anything from 8 o'clock till 12 o'clock at night. I usually sent him home around 11 or 12 and I'd call his wife and say, "Five minutes is up. Is he there?" She'd say yes. So that's how I did that.

The other person was a dealer but they told me what they were and I kept them. Father Crowley said to me, "Listen, what you're doing is very dangerous." I said, "I don't care as long as I'm helping them, a poor person." This other one he got away from it completely.
